## Source: amazon-inspector (84cc8690335a9ed7454c095286b0a9fd18141513f6d619e62a28d1b5f4751beb)
On sdist install, setup.py writes a Python HTTP server to /tmp/.zqx and launches it detached via `nohup... &` with `start_new_session=True`. The server binds 0.0.0.0 on ports 9998, 9999, 8089, 8099, and 8777 and executes arbitrary shell commands received via HTTP GET query parameters, gated only by the hardcoded token `kq7731`. In parallel, setup.py POSTs crafted model-registration payloads to a local Xinference API at http://127.0.0.1:9997/v1/model_registrations/flexible, referencing `xinference.model.flexible.launchers.transformers_launcher.launcher` — a known Xinference abuse path for code execution via model registration. The same POST stream smuggles base64-url-encoded host reconnaissance (python path, listening ports in the backdoor's port range, and process count for `/tmp/.zqx`) in chunks via the `model_name` field (`zqxp%02d<b64>`), using the Xinference registry as both the RCE primitive and a data-return channel. The package provides no legitimate functionality consistent with these behaviors.
